items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in cardiology clinic notes (3/13/2026, 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age 65-74, hypertension, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Current medications are levothyroxine and tamsulosin only; no anticoagulant order is active. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent - needs review (prior procedural hemorrhage is documented from a 2016 admission and should be weighed).

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 544 ms, up from 423 ms in 2020. Citalopram 40 mg daily - above the recommended maximum for QT reasons and a watch-list drug - remains current (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and Bazett QTc 561 ms (the 4/6/2022 tracing was atrial fibrillation with QTc 434 ms). Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (ordered 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug in a 95-year-old also on warfarin requires prescriber review; a repeat ECG is warranted as the last tracing is more than four years old.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started at the 11/10/2025 Cardiology Clinic visit, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window (due 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 560 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start predates 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start; QTc 434 ms. Requirement met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily was started at the 3/2/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo's 14-day window applies (due 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026 (5 days) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 375 ms. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit; because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 4/24/2026). The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - and no ECG was obtained by the due date, so the requirement was not met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was newly started at the 8/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit (the 2/18/2026 note listed only aspirin and atorvastatin), so an ECG was required within 14 days (due 8/15/2026). Her only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025; no ECG has been obtained since the start and the due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, requiring an ECG within 14 days (due 8/24/2026). The 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and there is no ECG for her in the chart. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the 9/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025, QTc 419 ms), but the due date falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, so an INR was required within 7 days (by 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window, so the requirement was met.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (female, age 65-74, hypertension, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia = 2 points). Current medications (6/23/2026 note): famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol; no anticoagulant order is current. Anticoagulation is strongly indicated.

On 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol after a reported home INR of 3.4, so a follow-up INR was required within 7 days (by 9/17/2026). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; the home INR of 3.4 preceded the dose change and cannot satisfy it. No INR has been obtained and the due date has passed.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes (1/28/2026, 5/2/2026, 8/4/2026) document paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy; hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for oral anticoagulation in men. Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline; no anticoagulant is ordered (prior long-term anticoagulant use is coded historically).

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in cardiology clinic notes (4/7/2026, 5/30/2026, 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (age >=75 = 2, female, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, atherosclerotic heart disease/old MI, prior cerebral infarction and TIA = 2). Only aspirin and gabapentin are current; no anticoagulant. High-risk untreated AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed on 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) even though outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 describe an 8/2-8/5/2026 admission for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting anticoagulation after major GI bleeding requires documented prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered the same day, valid to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 cardiology note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was re-issued rather than stopped, and the note still lists both. Clopidogrel is also current. Duplicate anticoagulation carries major bleeding risk.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day (17:13 and 19:36) show no organised P waves with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 130-145/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this materially affects anticoagulation and rate-control decisions.

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms, up from 359 ms on the prior tracing. Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and remains current (ordered 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 551 ms and Bazett QTc 560 ms, markedly increased from 421 ms on 6/7/2025 (amiodarone was started 11/10/2025). Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (ordered 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; he is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular rhythm with upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS at 81/min (mild respiratory RR variation). PR 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 323 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms. Frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. First ECG in the chart, so no comparison available. Confirms the same-day note of sinus rhythm.

7/15/2025. Sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II (PR about 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 100 ms, axis about +15 degrees, rS in V1 with R in V5-V6 and no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. The prior tracing (6/20/2025) showed a regular wide-complex tachycardia at 148/min with QRS about 140 ms (bundle branch block pattern) and QTc about 495 ms; the wide QRS has resolved and QTc has fallen by about 75 ms.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF (PR about 120 ms) and a small PR-segment deflection. QRS 94 ms, QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 436 ms. Frontal axis about +45 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison available.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves anywhere, irregularly irregular RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s (mean rate 136/min). No measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). Widespread T-wave inversion in I, II, V5-V6 consistent with rate-related repolarisation change; no bundle branch block. The tracing 2 h 23 min earlier (107914094) was also AF at about 132/min with QTc 435 ms, so no change. Note the same-day clinic note documents 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

8/2/2025. Regular rhythm at 69/min with a discrete low-amplitude atrial wave before every QRS (PR about 140 ms); the P vector is directed leftward/superiorly, matching the leftward QRS orientation. QRS 86 ms, QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Frontal axis about -28 degrees (within normal limits but borderline leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 4/27/2025 (61/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc 409 ms): no new AF/flutter, no new block, QTc change under 60 ms.

5/23/2024. Regular sinus rhythm at 98/min with upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR about 112 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, QT 298 ms, Bazett QTc 380 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

12/25/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min, low-amplitude but consistent upright P waves in II before each QRS, PR about 140 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 375 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. Frontal axis about +20 degrees. Deep S in V1-V2 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart. This tracing predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start - see the follow-up item.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.69-1.16 s, mean 61/min); no P waves are identifiable, so no PR interval. QRS 94 ms, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms (using mean RR). Frontal axis about +27 degrees. QS pattern in V1 with tall R in V6; no bundle branch block. The tracing three days earlier (11/12/2024) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves and PR 150 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new.

3/9/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 106 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 424 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Frontal axis about +60 degrees. Deep S in V1-V2, dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the previous day (106045460: 62/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc 452 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is under 60 ms. This is the baseline before haloperidol was started on 9/15/2026.

8/23/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 83/min with upright P waves in II/aVF, PR about 152 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms, QT 340 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Frontal axis about +55 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

6/19/2020. Regular sinus rhythm at 76/min with prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR about 158 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 443 ms. Frontal axis about +65 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2/2/2020 (sinus 75/min, QTc about 528 ms) the QTc has shortened by roughly 85 ms; QRS duration is also normal on both tracings.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, regular, with 1:1 upright P waves in II. PR 196 ms (upper normal, P and T nearly merge at this rate), QRS 96 ms, QT 279 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis about +45 degrees. No bundle branch block. Compared with 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 98 ms, QTc 401 ms) there is no new AF/flutter, no new conduction block and no significant QTc change.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular, with an upright P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms (RSR' configuration in V1 without terminal delay, so no right bundle branch block), QT 403 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Frontal axis about +33 degrees. Versus 11/30/2024 (51/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 368 ms): no new AF/flutter, no bundle branch block change and QTc change under 60 ms.

9/13/2025. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: absent P waves and markedly irregular RR intervals (0.29-0.58 s, mean 151/min); no PR interval measurable. QRS 104 ms, QT 270 ms, Bazett QTc 428 ms. Frontal axis about -11 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous day's tracing (9/12/2025) showed a regular rhythm at 77/min with atrial activity preceding each QRS and only isolated ectopy, so atrial fibrillation is new.

11/23/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 168 ms. QRS 94 ms, QT 353 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. Frontal axis about +5 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. This confirms the same-day note of 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'. Compared with 11/21/2025 (sinus 67/min, QT 503 ms, QTc 531 ms) the QTc has fallen by about 145 ms - a marked improvement in repolarisation.

2/15/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 74/min with broad upright P waves in I and II, PR about 188 ms (upper normal). QRS 90 ms with a small terminal positive deflection in V1 but no terminal delay, so no bundle branch block. QT 377 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms. Frontal axis about +35 degrees. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, strictly regular, with clear upright P waves in II and PR about 162 ms - no flutter waves on this tracing despite the coded history of atrial flutter. QRS 98 ms with a very deep S in V1 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for LVH) but no bundle branch block. QT 291 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms. Frontal axis about +40 degrees. Versus 7/4/2022 (sinus 115/min, QRS 98 ms, QTc 398 ms) the tracing is unchanged.

3/14/2025. Underlying regular sinus rhythm at 62/min with an upright P wave before each QRS (PR about 190 ms), interrupted by a single premature beat with a compensatory pause - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the coded paroxysmal AF. QRS 102 ms, QT about 375 ms, Bazett QTc about 380 ms. Frontal axis about -27 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

4/29/2026. Regular rhythm at 70/min with a consistent atrial wave 1:1 before each QRS (PR about 140 ms). The frontal plane vector is markedly abnormal: QRS and P are both negative in I and II and positive in III, giving an axis of about -175 degrees (extreme/north-west axis); limb-lead reversal or dextrocardia should be excluded clinically. QRS 92 ms, QT 357 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Precordial leads show rS in V1 with a modest R in V6 and no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison; it was recorded 19 days after escitalopram was started (see the follow-up item).

11/10/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 70/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 150 ms. QRS 106 ms - slightly widened but without a bundle branch block pattern (no terminal R' in V1, no broad monophasic R in V6). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged: QT 502 ms, Bazett QTc 544 ms. Frontal axis about +40 degrees. The prior tracing (6/17/2020, sinus tachycardia 132/min) had QTc 423 ms, so QTc has increased by about 120 ms. She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily - see the QT safety item.

3/8/2026. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 132 ms. QRS 86 ms with an Rs configuration in I/V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. QT about 410 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms - prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold. T waves are inverted in I, aVL and V2-V6. Frontal axis about +30 degrees by net QRS deflection. Only ECG in the chart; it satisfies the post-escitalopram monitoring requirement.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and PR about 160 ms. QRS 94 ms, QT 386 ms, Bazett QTc 363 ms. Frontal axis about -12 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 12/13/2018 (66/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 106 ms, QTc 388 ms): no new AF/flutter, no bundle branch block and QTc change well under 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 146 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc 359 ms, so QTc has risen by about 175 ms, well beyond the 60 ms threshold. He remains on escitalopram; see the QT safety review item.

7/13/2022. Regular narrow-to-borderline complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR fixed at 0.40-0.45 s) with a continuous sawtooth atrial baseline - negative deflections in II, III and aVF and positive deflections in V1 - at about 280-290/min, i.e. typical atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. No discrete P wave, so no PR interval. QRS 112 ms, QT about 262 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms (T-wave end is partly obscured by the flutter waves). Frontal axis about 0 degrees. No bundle branch block. The tracing two days earlier (7/11/2022) showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 105/min with no organised atrial activity, so the rhythm has organised into flutter.

5/12/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 82/min with upright P waves in II/aVF, PR about 154 ms. QRS 100 ms, QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 433 ms. Frontal axis about +28 degrees. rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

7/16/2022. Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 180 ms. Narrow QRS 80 ms, QT 333 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms. Net QRS gives a frontal axis of about -17 to -25 degrees (normal, leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 5/16/2021 (sinus 87/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc 395 ms): no new arrhythmia or block and QTc change under 60 ms.

7/17/2024. Sinus rhythm at 59/min with an upright P wave before each QRS but PR prolonged to about 232 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 134 ms with a deep broad QS in V1-V2, a broad monophasic R in I and V5-V6 and delayed intrinsicoid deflection - left bundle branch block. QT 436 ms, Bazett QTc 432 ms. Frontal axis about -28 degrees (normal, leftward). Compared with 6/3/2024 (sinus 68/min, identical LBBB with QRS 134 ms, PR about 210 ms, QTc 442 ms) there is no new or resolved block and no significant QTc change.

3/19/2025. Sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II and PR about 142 ms. QRS 92 ms with a late positive deflection in V1 but no terminal conduction delay, so no bundle branch block. QT 333 ms, Bazett QTc 433 ms. Frontal axis about +42 degrees. Versus the previous day (101016166: 101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc 430 ms) the tracing is unchanged.

9/22/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 66/min with upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR about 166 ms. QRS 92 ms. Net QRS is positive in I and negative in II, III and aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -33 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 373 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms. Low-voltage, largely isoelectric QRS in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm has been restored: regular rate 58/min with a discrete upright P wave in II (negative in V1) before every QRS, PR about 198 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with broad late T waves: QT 572 ms, Bazett QTc 561 ms. Frontal axis about +25 degrees. The prior tracing (4/6/2022) showed atrial fibrillation at about 130/min with QTc 434 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by about 125 ms (she is on amiodarone - see the QT safety item).

5/1/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, strictly regular, with upright P waves in II and PR about 162 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms, QT 307 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. Frontal axis about +45 degrees. Deep S in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 7/27/2019 (sinus 75/min, QRS 72 ms, QTc 423 ms): no new arrhythmia or block and no significant QTc change.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia, strictly regular at 121/min with small upright P waves in II before each QRS. PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 292 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. Frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal). rS in V1, tall R in V5-V6, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, clear upright P in II (PR 150 ms). QRS 92 ms, QT 320 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis about +55 degrees. Deep S in V1 with tall R in V5-V6; no conduction block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier (102910502: 100/min, QRS 92 ms, QTc 412 ms) - no new arrhythmia, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, strictly regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s) with an upright P before every QRS and no dropped beats despite the coded history of Mobitz II block. PR 166 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 438 ms, Bazett QTc 406 ms. Axis about +35 degrees; large-amplitude QRS with tall R in V5-V6. Versus 5/22/2023 (sinus 58/min with a single premature beat, QTc 384 ms): no new AF/flutter, no new block, QTc change under 60 ms.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, strictly regular, PR 130 ms. QRS has narrowed to 94 ms with loss of the terminal right-sided delay. Net QRS is negative in lead I and positive in III/aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +150 degrees (right axis deviation) with low limb-lead voltage. QT 293 ms, QTc 417 ms. The same-day earlier tracing (01:33) showed QRS 158 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S in I/V6 (right bundle branch block) and QTc about 475 ms; the block has resolved, and the QTc fall (about 57 ms) is just short of the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 62/min with 1:1 upright P waves, PR 174 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis about +50 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with broad late-peaking T waves: QT 551 ms, Bazett QTc 560 ms. The prior tracing (6/7/2025) showed sinus bradycardia 49/min with QTc 421 ms, so QTc has increased by about 140 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 11/10/2025. See the QT safety review item.

9/17/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.09 s, mean 101/min) with no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 84 ms, QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. Net QRS positive in I and negative in II, III and aVF gives a frontal axis of about -55 degrees (left axis deviation, left anterior fascicular pattern). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Clopidogrel is also current. Duplicate anticoagulation carries major bleeding risk.

The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this materially affects anticoagulation and rate-control decisions.

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 544 ms, up from 423 ms in 2020. Citalopram 40 mg daily - above the recommended maximum for QT reasons and a watch-list drug - remains current (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and Bazett QTc 561 ms (the 4/6/2022 tracing was atrial fibrillation with QTc 434 ms). Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (ordered 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug in a 95-year-old also on warfarin requires prescriber review; a repeat ECG is warranted as the last tracing is more than four years old.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started at the 11/10/2025 Cardiology Clinic visit, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window (due 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 560 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start predates 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start; QTc 434 ms. Requirement met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily was started at the 3/2/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo's 14-day window applies (due 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026 (5 days) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 375 ms. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit; because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 4/24/2026). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, requiring an ECG within 14 days (due 8/24/2026). Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the 9/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, so an INR was required within 7 days (by 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window, so the requirement was met.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (female, age 65-74, hypertension, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia = 2 points). Current medications (6/23/2026 note): famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol; no anticoagulant order is current. Anticoagulation is strongly indicated.

On 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol after a reported home INR of 3.4, so a follow-up INR was required within 7 days (by 9/17/2026). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; the home INR of 3.4 preceded the dose change and cannot satisfy it. No INR has been obtained and the due date has passed.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes (1/28/2026, 5/2/2026, 8/4/2026) document paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy; hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for oral anticoagulation in men. Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline; no anticoagulant is ordered (prior long-term anticoagulant use is coded historically).

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in cardiology clinic notes (4/7/2026, 5/30/2026, 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (age >=75 = 2, female, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, atherosclerotic heart disease/old MI, prior cerebral infarction and TIA = 2). Only aspirin and gabapentin are current; no anticoagulant. High-risk untreated AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed on 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) even though outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 describe an 8/2-8/5/2026 admission for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting anticoagulation after major GI bleeding requires documented prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered the same day, valid to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 cardiology note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was re-issued rather than stopped, and the note still lists both. Clopidogrel is also current. Duplicate anticoagulation carries major bleeding risk.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day (17:13 and 19:36) show no organised P waves with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 130-145/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this materially affects anticoagulation and rate-control decisions.

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms, up from 359 ms on the prior tracing. Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and remains current (ordered 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 551 ms and Bazett QTc 560 ms, markedly increased from 421 ms on 6/7/2025 (amiodarone was started 11/10/2025). Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (ordered 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; he is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular rhythm with upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS at 81/min (mild respiratory RR variation). PR 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 323 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms. Frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. First ECG in the chart, so no comparison available. Confirms the same-day note of sinus rhythm.

7/15/2025. Sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II (PR about 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 100 ms, axis about +15 degrees, rS in V1 with R in V5-V6 and no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. The prior tracing (6/20/2025) showed a regular wide-complex tachycardia at 148/min with QRS about 140 ms (bundle branch block pattern) and QTc about 495 ms; the wide QRS has resolved and QTc has fallen by about 75 ms.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF (PR about 120 ms) and a small PR-segment deflection. QRS 94 ms, QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 436 ms. Frontal axis about +45 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison available.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves anywhere, irregularly irregular RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s (mean rate 136/min). No measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). Widespread T-wave inversion in I, II, V5-V6 consistent with rate-related repolarisation change; no bundle branch block. The tracing 2 h 23 min earlier (107914094) was also AF at about 132/min with QTc 435 ms, so no change. Note the same-day clinic note documents 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

8/2/2025. Regular rhythm at 69/min with a discrete low-amplitude atrial wave before every QRS (PR about 140 ms); the P vector is directed leftward/superiorly, matching the leftward QRS orientation. QRS 86 ms, QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Frontal axis about -28 degrees (within normal limits but borderline leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 4/27/2025 (61/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc 409 ms): no new AF/flutter, no new block, QTc change under 60 ms.

5/23/2024. Regular sinus rhythm at 98/min with upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR about 112 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, QT 298 ms, Bazett QTc 380 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, regular, with 1:1 upright P waves in II. PR 196 ms (upper normal, P and T nearly merge at this rate), QRS 96 ms, QT 279 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis about +45 degrees. No bundle branch block. Compared with 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 98 ms, QTc 401 ms) there is no new AF/flutter, no new conduction block and no significant QTc change.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 146 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc 359 ms, so QTc has risen by about 175 ms, well beyond the 60 ms threshold. He remains on escitalopram; see the QT safety review item.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia, strictly regular at 121/min with small upright P waves in II before each QRS. PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 292 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. Frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal). rS in V1, tall R in V5-V6, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, clear upright P in II (PR 150 ms). QRS 92 ms, QT 320 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis about +55 degrees. Deep S in V1 with tall R in V5-V6; no conduction block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier (102910502: 100/min, QRS 92 ms, QTc 412 ms) - no new arrhythmia, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, strictly regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s) with an upright P before every QRS and no dropped beats despite the coded history of Mobitz II block. PR 166 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 438 ms, Bazett QTc 406 ms. Axis about +35 degrees; large-amplitude QRS with tall R in V5-V6. Versus 5/22/2023 (sinus 58/min with a single premature beat, QTc 384 ms): no new AF/flutter, no new block, QTc change under 60 ms.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, strictly regular, PR 130 ms. QRS has narrowed to 94 ms with loss of the terminal right-sided delay. Net QRS is negative in lead I and positive in III/aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +150 degrees (right axis deviation) with low limb-lead voltage. QT 293 ms, QTc 417 ms. The same-day earlier tracing (01:33) showed QRS 158 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S in I/V6 (right bundle branch block) and QTc about 475 ms; the block has resolved, and the QTc fall (about 57 ms) is just short of the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 62/min with 1:1 upright P waves, PR 174 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis about +50 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with broad late-peaking T waves: QT 551 ms, Bazett QTc 560 ms. The prior tracing (6/7/2025) showed sinus bradycardia 49/min with QTc 421 ms, so QTc has increased by about 140 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 11/10/2025. See the QT safety review item.

9/17/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.09 s, mean 101/min) with no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 84 ms, QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. Net QRS positive in I and negative in II, III and aVF gives a frontal axis of about -55 degrees (left axis deviation, left anterior fascicular pattern). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent - needs review (prior procedural hemorrhage is documented from a 2016 admission and should be weighed).

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 544 ms, up from 423 ms in 2020. Citalopram 40 mg daily - above the recommended maximum for QT reasons and a watch-list drug - remains current (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and Bazett QTc 561 ms (the 4/6/2022 tracing was atrial fibrillation with QTc 434 ms). Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (ordered 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug in a 95-year-old also on warfarin requires prescriber review; a repeat ECG is warranted as the last tracing is more than four years old.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started at the 11/10/2025 Cardiology Clinic visit, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window (due 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 560 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start predates 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start; QTc 434 ms. Requirement met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily was started at the 3/2/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo's 14-day window applies (due 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026 (5 days) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 375 ms. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit; because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 4/24/2026). The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - and no ECG was obtained by the due date, so the requirement was not met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was newly started at the 8/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit (the 2/18/2026 note listed only aspirin and atorvastatin), so an ECG was required within 14 days (due 8/15/2026). Her only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025; no ECG has been obtained since the start and the due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, requiring an ECG within 14 days (due 8/24/2026). The 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and there is no ECG for her in the chart. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the 9/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025, QTc 419 ms), but the due date falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, so an INR was required within 7 days (by 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window, so the requirement was met.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (female, age 65-74, hypertension, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia = 2 points). Current medications (6/23/2026 note): famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol; no anticoagulant order is current. Anticoagulation is strongly indicated.

On 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol after a reported home INR of 3.4, so a follow-up INR was required within 7 days (by 9/17/2026). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; the home INR of 3.4 preceded the dose change and cannot satisfy it. No INR has been obtained and the due date has passed.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes (1/28/2026, 5/2/2026, 8/4/2026) document paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy; hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for oral anticoagulation in men. Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline; no anticoagulant is ordered (prior long-term anticoagulant use is coded historically).

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in cardiology clinic notes (4/7/2026, 5/30/2026, 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (age >=75 = 2, female, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, atherosclerotic heart disease/old MI, prior cerebral infarction and TIA = 2). Only aspirin and gabapentin are current; no anticoagulant. High-risk untreated AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed on 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) even though outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 describe an 8/2-8/5/2026 admission for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting anticoagulation after major GI bleeding requires documented prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered the same day, valid to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 cardiology note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was re-issued rather than stopped, and the note still lists both. Clopidogrel is also current. Duplicate anticoagulation carries major bleeding risk.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day (17:13 and 19:36) show no organised P waves with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 130-145/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this materially affects anticoagulation and rate-control decisions.

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms, up from 359 ms on the prior tracing. Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and remains current (ordered 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 551 ms and Bazett QTc 560 ms, markedly increased from 421 ms on 6/7/2025 (amiodarone was started 11/10/2025). Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (ordered 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; he is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular rhythm with upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS at 81/min (mild respiratory RR variation). PR 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 323 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms. Frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. First ECG in the chart, so no comparison available. Confirms the same-day note of sinus rhythm.

7/15/2025. Sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II (PR about 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 100 ms, axis about +15 degrees, rS in V1 with R in V5-V6 and no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. The prior tracing (6/20/2025) showed a regular wide-complex tachycardia at 148/min with QRS about 140 ms (bundle branch block pattern) and QTc about 495 ms; the wide QRS has resolved and QTc has fallen by about 75 ms.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF (PR about 120 ms) and a small PR-segment deflection. QRS 94 ms, QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 436 ms. Frontal axis about +45 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison available.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves anywhere, irregularly irregular RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s (mean rate 136/min). No measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). Widespread T-wave inversion in I, II, V5-V6 consistent with rate-related repolarisation change; no bundle branch block. The tracing 2 h 23 min earlier (107914094) was also AF at about 132/min with QTc 435 ms, so no change. Note the same-day clinic note documents 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

8/2/2025. Regular rhythm at 69/min with a discrete low-amplitude atrial wave before every QRS (PR about 140 ms); the P vector is directed leftward/superiorly, matching the leftward QRS orientation. QRS 86 ms, QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Frontal axis about -28 degrees (within normal limits but borderline leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 4/27/2025 (61/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc 409 ms): no new AF/flutter, no new block, QTc change under 60 ms.

5/23/2024. Regular sinus rhythm at 98/min with upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR about 112 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, QT 298 ms, Bazett QTc 380 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

12/25/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min, low-amplitude but consistent upright P waves in II before each QRS, PR about 140 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 375 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. Frontal axis about +20 degrees. Deep S in V1-V2 with dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart. This tracing predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start - see the follow-up item.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.69-1.16 s, mean 61/min); no P waves are identifiable, so no PR interval. QRS 94 ms, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms (using mean RR). Frontal axis about +27 degrees. QS pattern in V1 with tall R in V6; no bundle branch block. The tracing three days earlier (11/12/2024) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves and PR 150 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new.

3/9/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 106 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 424 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Frontal axis about +60 degrees. Deep S in V1-V2, dominant R in V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the previous day (106045460: 62/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc 452 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is under 60 ms. This is the baseline before haloperidol was started on 9/15/2026.

8/23/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 83/min with upright P waves in II/aVF, PR about 152 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms, QT 340 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Frontal axis about +55 degrees (normal). rS in V1 with dominant R in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

6/19/2020. Regular sinus rhythm at 76/min with prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR about 158 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 443 ms. Frontal axis about +65 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2/2/2020 (sinus 75/min, QTc about 528 ms) the QTc has shortened by roughly 85 ms; QRS duration is also normal on both tracings.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, regular, with 1:1 upright P waves in II. PR 196 ms (upper normal, P and T nearly merge at this rate), QRS 96 ms, QT 279 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis about +45 degrees. No bundle branch block. Compared with 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 98 ms, QTc 401 ms) there is no new AF/flutter, no new conduction block and no significant QTc change.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular, with an upright P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms (RSR' configuration in V1 without terminal delay, so no right bundle branch block), QT 403 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Frontal axis about +33 degrees. Versus 11/30/2024 (51/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 368 ms): no new AF/flutter, no bundle branch block change and QTc change under 60 ms.

9/13/2025. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: absent P waves and markedly irregular RR intervals (0.29-0.58 s, mean 151/min); no PR interval measurable. QRS 104 ms, QT 270 ms, Bazett QTc 428 ms. Frontal axis about -11 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous day's tracing (9/12/2025) showed a regular rhythm at 77/min with atrial activity preceding each QRS and only isolated ectopy, so atrial fibrillation is new.

11/23/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 168 ms. QRS 94 ms, QT 353 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. Frontal axis about +5 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. This confirms the same-day note of 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'. Compared with 11/21/2025 (sinus 67/min, QT 503 ms, QTc 531 ms) the QTc has fallen by about 145 ms - a marked improvement in repolarisation.

2/15/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 74/min with broad upright P waves in I and II, PR about 188 ms (upper normal). QRS 90 ms with a small terminal positive deflection in V1 but no terminal delay, so no bundle branch block. QT 377 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms. Frontal axis about +35 degrees. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, strictly regular, with clear upright P waves in II and PR about 162 ms - no flutter waves on this tracing despite the coded history of atrial flutter. QRS 98 ms with a very deep S in V1 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for LVH) but no bundle branch block. QT 291 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms. Frontal axis about +40 degrees. Versus 7/4/2022 (sinus 115/min, QRS 98 ms, QTc 398 ms) the tracing is unchanged.

3/14/2025. Underlying regular sinus rhythm at 62/min with an upright P wave before each QRS (PR about 190 ms), interrupted by a single premature beat with a compensatory pause - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the coded paroxysmal AF. QRS 102 ms, QT about 375 ms, Bazett QTc about 380 ms. Frontal axis about -27 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

4/29/2026. Regular rhythm at 70/min with a consistent atrial wave 1:1 before each QRS (PR about 140 ms). The frontal plane vector is markedly abnormal: QRS and P are both negative in I and II and positive in III, giving an axis of about -175 degrees (extreme/north-west axis); limb-lead reversal or dextrocardia should be excluded clinically. QRS 92 ms, QT 357 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Precordial leads show rS in V1 with a modest R in V6 and no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison; it was recorded 19 days after escitalopram was started (see the follow-up item).

11/10/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 70/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 150 ms. QRS 106 ms - slightly widened but without a bundle branch block pattern (no terminal R' in V1, no broad monophasic R in V6). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged: QT 502 ms, Bazett QTc 544 ms. Frontal axis about +40 degrees. The prior tracing (6/17/2020, sinus tachycardia 132/min) had QTc 423 ms, so QTc has increased by about 120 ms. She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily - see the QT safety item.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 146 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT 502 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc 359 ms, so QTc has risen by about 175 ms, well beyond the 60 ms threshold. He remains on escitalopram; see the QT safety review item.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia, strictly regular at 121/min with small upright P waves in II before each QRS. PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 292 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. Frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal). rS in V1, tall R in V5-V6, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, clear upright P in II (PR 150 ms). QRS 92 ms, QT 320 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis about +55 degrees. Deep S in V1 with tall R in V5-V6; no conduction block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier (102910502: 100/min, QRS 92 ms, QTc 412 ms) - no new arrhythmia, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, strictly regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s) with an upright P before every QRS and no dropped beats despite the coded history of Mobitz II block. PR 166 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 438 ms, Bazett QTc 406 ms. Axis about +35 degrees; large-amplitude QRS with tall R in V5-V6. Versus 5/22/2023 (sinus 58/min with a single premature beat, QTc 384 ms): no new AF/flutter, no new block, QTc change under 60 ms.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, strictly regular, PR 130 ms. QRS has narrowed to 94 ms with loss of the terminal right-sided delay. Net QRS is negative in lead I and positive in III/aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +150 degrees (right axis deviation) with low limb-lead voltage. QT 293 ms, QTc 417 ms. The same-day earlier tracing (01:33) showed QRS 158 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S in I/V6 (right bundle branch block) and QTc about 475 ms; the block has resolved, and the QTc fall (about 57 ms) is just short of the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 62/min with 1:1 upright P waves, PR 174 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis about +50 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with broad late-peaking T waves: QT 551 ms, Bazett QTc 560 ms. The prior tracing (6/7/2025) showed sinus bradycardia 49/min with QTc 421 ms, so QTc has increased by about 140 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 11/10/2025. See the QT safety review item.

9/17/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.09 s, mean 101/min) with no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 84 ms, QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. Net QRS positive in I and negative in II, III and aVF gives a frontal axis of about -55 degrees (left axis deviation, left anterior fascicular pattern). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

arguments.explanation: 3/8/2026. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min with upright P waves in II, PR about 132 ms. QRS 86 ms with an Rs configuration in I/V5-V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. QT about 410 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms - prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold. T waves are inverted in I, aVL and V2-V6. Frontal axis about +30 degrees by net QRS deflection. Only ECG in the chart; it satisfies the post-escitalopram monitoring requirement.
